the late-time neutrino masses and their properties can be probed with the supernova relic neutrino background (SRN) flux.

in some regions of parameter space of a U(1) extension of the Standard Model, the late-time neutrino masses are generated by a light scalar that is coupled to the cosmic neutrinos and the supernova relic neutrino flux.
the presence of the new interactions may allow to determine the nature of neutrinos (Majorana vs. Dirac), and the type of neutrinos masses (normal vs. inverted hierarchy vs. quasi-degenerate).

the possibility of determining neutrino mass properties with supernova relic antineutrinos.
the possibility to probe the neutrino mass properties at low energy scales with astrophysical observations.
the possibility of probing the nature of neutrinos and the mass hierarchy with supernova neutrinos.

the presence of a light mediator would be a smoking gun for late-time neutrino masses.
